body:
claimed: Hermes Coder - 2026-11-08 - branch issue/260-facing-gap. Owner assignment: "Intake and complete a camcraft issue". Intake transferred from #241 after native reproduction showed that its saved Trace/Contour generate successfully and its facing failure is exactly this report.

Plan: inspect the original vs radius-grown cutout boundaries and clipped row at Y=-55.50; correct the specific gap/refusal logic, preserving swept-area leftover diagnostics and real too-narrow-strip refusals. Add a compact regression plus generation checks on the public project, and explicitly establish fixture preconditions. A missing row alone is not evidence that the horizontal gap is narrower than the tool; determine whether concave neighbouring edges legitimately exclude it. Expected files are motion machining2d/face_holes.rs, its caller in face.rs, focused motion tests and an app regression fixture only as needed. No new dependencies, schema, architecture, selection UX, box picker, host changes, releases or machine-output transfer.

Validation and delegation: one isolated leaf verifier owns native test execution (baseline sensitivity, pinning tests, quick gate, affected motion Clippy -D warnings); a separate bounded reviewer checks the frozen diff; a leaf support task writes the per-issue decision record. Parent implements and integrates. Native branch starts at current fetched main 8f30beec98d74443a914b872f4e91c620c459dc3. Publish only the approved feature branch to owner fork, draft first, then ready after gates; no protected-main merge. Broader #241 GUI symptom is not claimed fixed. Existing #261 covers showing failed toolpaths, outside this change.

Root cause confirmed: the reported 15.1455 mm horizontal gap is a concave notch within ONE cutout, not a strip between two separate holes. At Y=-55.50 its crossings are X=-117.57277 and -102.42723; the nearby return edge peaks at Y=-55.00. Points across that gap lie less than 0.5 mm from the return. Expanding that hole by the tool's 1.5 mm radius therefore correctly excludes the row. The clipping is not broken and must remain unchanged.

Patch: narrow-gap rejection now also requires gap <= tool diameter (equality remains conservative); the diagnostic says no wider than the tool. Wider missing pieces keep the existing swept-area unfaced-material note instead. Added a compact U-hole regression in both cutting directions and an exactly-tool-width refusal test; existing genuinely narrow-gap coverage is retained. Candidate code tree: 13788b35b3c3edc3ca935737c762f060d58e4c4e. Native sensitivity, focused gates and real-project confirmation are delegated; no pass is claimed yet. #241 is released and remains open because its broader GUI symptom was not reproduced.

Validation checkpoint and narrow plan correction: the first width guard passed the local quick gate but did not finish the real project: a later row at Y=54.00 reports a 2.65 mm gap. That gap's two crossings are on the SAME cutout boundary too. The width-only patch was incomplete; no PR was submitted.

The correction now keeps each crossing's boundary identity. The refusal about material between two holes applies only to distinct boundaries with a missing row piece and gap <= cutter diameter. Concave returns within one boundary, whether wider or narrower than the cutter, remain clipped and are measured by the existing swept-area unfaced note. No path is driven through a hole and the verifier is unchanged. A new 2 mm U-notch regression supplements the 4 mm notch and true between-hole equality/refusal controls. The earlier style failure used rustfmt's default edition; checks must use the repository's Rust 2024 edition, as the formatting invocation already did.

Current main advanced to 1e60b2399dff677d9f44b143a24e626d268340f0. Relevant patch paths and controlling AGENTS are unchanged; the patch is forward-ported in a fresh isolated worktree before final gates. New code tree: 7a6fa78d29c215d61ab2cde867f6f4341d892824. The issue #260 attachment was also downloaded independently and matches the earlier fixture SHA-256 exactly. Native public-project verification will run before the wider quick gate so another real failure is not hidden by smaller fixtures. Owner explicitly resumed this existing work after a tool approval timeout.

The real-project check now passes on the boundary-aware correction: Trace 1060 moves, Lift facing 725, Through control 101, Contour 679. Lift retains the explicit 1653.05 mm^2 unfaced-area note and the lift-over-holes note. These are generation results, not real-machine or full-coverage acceptance; existing rotated-stock/rapid-law diagnostics remain visible in the logs.

The three compact regressions, prior-code sensitivity, motion Clippy -D warnings, Rust-2024 formatting check and independent static review have been verified. The code is committed and pushed to seelesturm/Camcraft branch issue/260-facing-gap at b3dd4934090d6d30e17a1130939f6789799f8f2a (tree 3d36ac1b75e3224022cdead91dbd77ad22baa366).

Final parent readback found the quick-gate wrapper's exit-zero receipt lacks the expected gate-created logs and executed-test summaries. That gate is unverified until direct capture supplies the actual plan, assertion counts and native exit. Only this missing gate is being recovered; the passed independent checks are not being repeated. No PR is open yet and no merge or release was performed.

fix on issue/260-facing-gap (seelesturm/Camcraft) - PR #313: https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/313

Validated commit b3dd4934090d6d30e17a1130939f6789799f8f2a, tree 3d36ac1b75e3224022cdead91dbd77ad22baa366. The recovered canonical quick gate has actual gate-created logs and native exit 0: 173 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored. This supersedes the earlier unverified wrapper receipt. Motion Clippy -D warnings, Rust-2024 formatting/whitespace checks, prior-code sensitivity, and independent static review also passed.

Pinned by a_wide_concave_gap_generates_and_reports_the_unfaced_return, a_narrow_concave_return_is_not_a_gap_between_separate_holes, and a_gap_exactly_one_tool_wide_still_refuses_when_no_row_piece_fits; genuine narrow-between-hole coverage remains.

The original attachment generates Lift facing with 725 moves and explicit notes for 1653.05 mm^2 left unfaced and lift-over-hole behavior. Trace/Through/Contour controls also generate; existing stock/rapid-law diagnostics are retained. This is not full material coverage, GUI/platform qualification, or real-machine acceptance. No workflows, releases, merges, or machine transfers were performed.

PR opened as a draft, then flagged ready after the final-head gates and independent review. Ready for maintainer review and manual merge; no further branch pushes are planned. #241 remains open for its unreproduced broader selection symptoms.
